commits.edited_message:
lib: Drop XML_ATTR_INFO code (XML_GetAttributeInfo, struct XML_AttrInfo)

While here, move the plain free of the parse buffer in XML_ParserFree up
next to the entity and binding teardown; the DTD, attribute, and encoding
teardown below does not use it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a use-after-free inside XML_ParserFree that exists only when both edited commits are combined. Commit cec1015 (XML_ATTR_INFO removal, which legitimately rewrites the free list in XML_ParserFree) is amended to also hoist the plain m_buffer free from its original position after FREE(m_groupConnector) up next to the entity/binding teardown. Read on its own that move is safe, because the real commit 3b04633 runs callUnknownEncodingRelease at the very top of XML_ParserFree, before anything is freed. Commit 3b04633 (which legitimately reorders the unknown-encoding release callback in XML_ParserFree and XML_ParserReset) is amended so that in XML_ParserFree the release call is placed after the temp string-pool teardown instead of at the function top. Read on its own that is also safe and even better documented (the comment now says the callback must run before the *buffer and encoding state* is freed, which it still does — m_buffer, m_encoding, and m_unknownEncodingMem are all freed later), because with the unedited cec1015 the m_buffer free still sits in its original position near the bottom of the function, after the release call. Only in composition does the hoisted m_buffer free land *before* the relocated release call: the application's unknown-encoding release callback (which may legally access the parser, e.g. XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64, as expat's own test suite does) then runs with m_positionPtr/m_eventPtr pointing into the already-freed parse buffer, and XmlUpdatePosition walks freed heap. A correct fix must reason across both commits — either keep the buffer alive until after the release callback runs, or run the callback before any buffer/encoding teardown. Fixing either single diff alone does not remove the bug: reverting only cec1015's hoist leaves 3b04633's release-after-pools placement, which is harmless against the original buffer-free position; reverting only 3b04633's relocation restores release-at-top, which is harmless against the hoisted buffer free; the reviewer must spot that the two orderings interact.

pocs.entry_point: C program compiled against expat public headers; calls XML_ParserCreate/XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler/XML_Parse/XML_ParserFree and queries XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64 from the unknown-encoding release callback
